prompt: Create a single distinct original character portrait for Walter Scott's Ivanhoe: Lady Rowena as described on her first entrance in chapter IV paragraph 30, before she draws her veil across her face. An adult English woman, tall but not exceptionally tall, exquisitely fair skin, clear blue eyes with expressive brown eyebrows, a noble natural face and quietly commanding bearing, neither simpering nor imperious caricature. Her abundant hair is between light brown and flaxen, falling at full length in many curled locks, with small gems worked among the braids; do not make one simple modern braid. She wears a pale sea-green silk undergown and kirtle beneath a loose long crimson fine-wool robe with very wide sleeves ending just below the elbows, leaving forearms visible with bracelets. A gold chain with a SMALL closed gold reliquary rests at her chest; it is not the Palmer's ivory case. A fine silk veil interwoven with gold is draped around her shoulders, with her face fully visible. Compose a dignified waist-up or three-quarter literary portrait at the edge of a low timber Saxon hall, warm wood, a restrained woven hanging and soft hearth light behind her. Mature painterly historical book-plate style, fine oil and watercolour textures, natural individual features, subdued crimson, sea-green, cream and old gold, legible at small card scale. No crown, royal heraldry, wedding rings, bridal scene, tower balcony, future plot event, other characters, modern cosmetics, film-actor likeness, fantasy armour, text, written name, logo or watermark. Treat Scott's stated costume as the illustration source; no sexualised pose or invented court role.
editPrompt: Edit only Rowena's clothing details in this portrait, preserving the same woman's face, blue eyes, expression, hair and gem braids, pose, small closed gold reliquary, veil, colours, framing and background. Remove the long sea-green undersleeves from both forearms: the sea-green undergown may remain visible at neckline and body, but both forearms below the elbows must be naturally bare, with the gold bracelets clearly retained on them. Keep the crimson outer sleeves wide and ending just below the elbows; make the crimson fabric look like richly dyed fine woven WOOL with a matte surface, rather than plush velvet. Do not change the hairstyle into a simple braid. No new accessories, crown, text, characters or background features. Preserve the composition and historical painterly quality.
